programme.displayName: RDS, EC2, and Application Load Balancer Follow Along
programme.subtitle: Build and validate a three-tier SAA-C03 practice architecture: internet → Application Load Balancer → EC2 → private RDS for MySQL.
programme.description: In Europe (London) (eu-west-2), use an existing VPC that has subnets in at least two Availability Zones. Create separate security groups for an internet-facing Application Load Balancer, EC2 web targets, and a private RDS for MySQL DB instance. Deploy a simple HTTP workload behind the ALB, validate target health and traffic distribution, then verify the private EC2-to-RDS network path.
programme.learningOutcome: Build, verify, monitor, troubleshoot, and manually clean up an internet-facing Application Load Balancer that forwards HTTP traffic to EC2 targets while a private RDS for MySQL DB instance accepts port 3306 traffic only from the EC2 security group. Recognize SAA-C03 scenarios that call for ALB, security-group references, private database placement, Multi-AZ deployments, read replicas, and Auto Scaling.

phases.title: Prepare identity, tools, and the existing VPC
phases.description: Use a non-root identity, configure the AWS CLI for eu-west-2, and identify the VPC and subnet layout needed by the ALB, EC2, and RDS tiers.

phases.title: Build the private network access chain
phases.description: Create separate security groups and apply security-group references so that each tier accepts traffic only from the tier immediately in front of it.

phases.title: Validate, monitor, scale, troubleshoot, and review SAA-C03 choices

tasks.title: Use a non-root identity and configure AWS CLI access
tasks.goal: Use a dedicated non-root learning identity or approved IAM Identity Center identity, configure AWS CLI access, set eu-west-2, and confirm the active AWS account identity.
tasks.whyItMatters: For SAA-C03, root credentials should not be used for normal work. Exam wording such as “least privilege,” “temporary credentials,” “centralized workforce access,” or “do not use root” should make you consider IAM Identity Center, IAM roles, and narrowly scoped permissions. This Follow Along requires permissions to inspect and create the listed EC2, ELBv2, RDS, CloudWatch, Systems Manager, Secrets Manager, and IAM-instance-profile resources. Use an administrator-approved learning identity with only the permissions needed in this account; do not create or attach a custom IAM policy in this Follow Along.

tasks.title: Inspect the VPC and select ALB, EC2, and DB subnets
tasks.goal: Record one existing VPC ID and identify subnets in at least two Availability Zones for the ALB and DB subnet group, plus a suitable EC2 subnet.
tasks.whyItMatters: An Application Load Balancer requires at least two enabled Availability Zones. An RDS DB subnet group must cover at least two Availability Zones so that the DB can support Multi-AZ deployment. SAA-C03 questions mentioning “high availability across Availability Zones,” “internet-facing ALB,” or “private database” should make you inspect subnet routing and placement before launching resources.

tasks.title: Create the ALB, EC2, and RDS security-group chain
tasks.goal: Create three separate security groups and allow only internet → ALB on HTTP, ALB → EC2 on HTTP, and EC2 → RDS on MySQL port 3306.
tasks.whyItMatters: Security groups are stateful and can reference another security group as a source. That makes them appropriate for tier-to-tier access controls that survive changing private IP addresses. In SAA-C03 questions, phrases such as “only the application servers may reach the database” usually point to a security-group reference instead of an IP CIDR rule.

consoleSteps.title: Create the ALB group
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The ALB security group exists.
consoleSteps.warning: Use a separate group for the internet-facing ALB.

consoleSteps.title: Allow public HTTP to the ALB
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Add inbound HTTP from 0.0.0.0/0 to fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg.

instructions.text: ☐ Add inbound HTTP from 0.0.0.0/0 to fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The ALB can receive temporary HTTP test traffic from the internet.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not add this public rule to the EC2 or RDS security group.

consoleSteps.title: Create the web group
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The EC2 web security group exists.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not add public HTTP or SSH access to this group.

consoleSteps.title: Allow ALB-to-EC2 HTTP
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Add inbound HTTP from fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg to fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg.

instructions.text: ☐ Add inbound HTTP from fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg to fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Only resources using the ALB group can initiate HTTP traffic to EC2.
consoleSteps.warning: Choose the ALB security group as the source instead of a public CIDR.

consoleSteps.title: Create the RDS group
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The RDS security group exists.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not attach this group to the ALB or EC2 web targets.

consoleSteps.title: Allow EC2-to-RDS MySQL
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Add inbound MySQL port 3306 from fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg to fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg.

instructions.text: ☐ Add inbound MySQL port 3306 from fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg to fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Only EC2 instances using the web security group can initiate MySQL traffic to RDS.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not use 0.0.0.0/0 or an individual instance IP address for this rule.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg --description "ALB HTTP security group for Follow Along" --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [VPC_ID] and record the returned GroupId as [ALB_SG_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the ALB security-group ID.
cliSteps.warning: Security-group names must be unique within the VPC.

cliSteps.explanation: Replace [ALB_SG_ID]. This permits public HTTP only to the ALB tier.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response confirms the ingress rule.
cliSteps.warning: This is intentionally temporary and applies only to the ALB group.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg --description "Web tier HTTP from ALB only" --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [VPC_ID] and record the returned GroupId as [WEB_SG_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the EC2 web security-group ID.
cliSteps.warning: Do not reuse the ALB security group for the web tier.

cliSteps.explanation: Replace both group ID placeholders. This creates the ALB-to-EC2 security-group reference.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The web-group inbound rule lists the ALB security group as its source.
cliSteps.warning: The rule allows private-IP traffic from network interfaces using the referenced ALB group.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg --description "Private RDS MySQL from web tier only" --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [VPC_ID] and record the returned GroupId as [RDS_SG_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the RDS security-group ID.
cliSteps.warning: Do not use this group for client or load-balancer traffic.

cliSteps.explanation: Replace both group ID placeholders. This permits MySQL network traffic only from resources using the EC2 web group.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The RDS-group inbound rule lists [WEB_SG_ID] on TCP 3306.
cliSteps.warning: Security-group authorization is network authorization; MySQL authentication remains separately required.

verification.title: Confirm the three-hop inbound chain
verification.instruction: Inspect the inbound rules and confirm: 0.0.0.0/0 → ALB TCP 80, ALB SG → web SG TCP 80, and web SG → RDS SG TCP 3306.
verification.expectedResult: Neither the web SG nor the RDS SG accepts direct public inbound traffic.

verification.title: Explain stateful behavior
verification.instruction: Confirm that the return traffic for an allowed connection does not require a matching inbound rule because security groups are stateful.
verification.expectedResult: You can distinguish stateful security groups from subnet-level network ACLs.

cleanup.description: After all dependent ALB, EC2, and RDS resources are deleted, manually delete only fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg, fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg, and fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg.

SAA-C03 wording such as “replace unhealthy servers,” “distribute traffic,” or “avoid direct public access to backend servers” should make you consider an ALB with multiple targets and, in production, an Auto Scaling group.

tasks.title: Create the target group and internet-facing Application Load Balancer
tasks.goal: Create an HTTP instance target group, register the first EC2 target, create an internet-facing ALB in two Availability Zones, and forward listener traffic to the target group.
tasks.whyItMatters: ALB operates at Layer 7 and uses listeners, listener rules, target groups, and health checks. Exam wording mentioning host-based routing, path-based routing, HTTP headers, web applications, or a public HTTP(S) entry point should make you consider ALB. Choose Network Load Balancer instead when the workload needs Layer 4 TCP/UDP/TLS behavior, static IP addresses, or extreme connection performance rather than HTTP-aware routing.

tasks.title: Create the DB subnet group and private RDS for MySQL DB instance
tasks.goal: Create a DB subnet group across two Availability Zones and create a non-public RDS for MySQL DB instance with the RDS security group, backup retention, and a Multi-AZ-ready subnet design.
tasks.whyItMatters: A private RDS DB instance keeps the database off the public internet while allowing the EC2 application tier to reach it through a security-group reference. For SAA-C03, “automatic failover,” “higher availability,” and “standby that does not serve reads” point to Multi-AZ. “Scale read-heavy workload” points to read replicas. “Managed relational database with higher compatibility and availability options” can also suggest Aurora, while bursty or serverless workloads may call for Aurora Serverless or serverless application designs.

consoleSteps.title: Open RDS
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The RDS console opens in eu-west-2.
consoleSteps.warning: Keep the Region set to Europe (London).

consoleSteps.title: Create the DB subnet group

tasks.title: Verify ALB target health, browser traffic, and private RDS access
tasks.feature: ALB health checks and RDS connectivity
tasks.goal: Verify healthy EC2 targets, open the ALB DNS name, confirm the database endpoint and security-group chain, and use Session Manager only when an approved EC2 instance profile already exists.
tasks.whyItMatters: ALB routes traffic only to healthy targets in enabled Availability Zones. An unhealthy target often results from a wrong health-check path, an unavailable web service, incorrect port, a target in an unavailable AZ, or a web security group that does not permit ALB traffic. For SAA-C03, troubleshooting language about “502/503,” “unhealthy target,” “health check,” or “backend only reachable through the load balancer” should direct you to these checks.

tasks.title: Add a second target and observe load distribution and graceful deregistration
tasks.goal: Add a second EC2 web target in another Availability Zone, observe that both targets become healthy, and practice graceful deregistration.
tasks.whyItMatters: ALB distributes requests across healthy registered targets. Registering targets in multiple enabled Availability Zones improves resilience, but production replacement should usually be automated with an Auto Scaling group rather than manual instance launches. Exam wording such as “replace failed instances automatically,” “scale out,” or “maintain capacity across AZs” should make you consider EC2 Auto Scaling behind an ALB.

tasks.title: Practice safe ALB and RDS troubleshooting
tasks.goal: Create controlled failures, observe evidence, restore the original configuration, and distinguish network failures from database credential failures.
tasks.whyItMatters: Troubleshooting questions on SAA-C03 often require identifying the narrowest broken layer. A bad ALB health-check path produces an unhealthy target; an ALB security-group problem blocks clients; a web-group source problem blocks ALB-to-EC2 traffic; an RDS-group rule problem blocks EC2-to-RDS traffic. Incorrect MySQL credentials and an incorrect DNS endpoint are different failures from security-group blocks.

instructions.text: ☐ Set the target-group health-check path to /missing.

consoleSteps.warning: This is an intentional temporary failure; record the reason before restoring the path.

consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Set the target-group health-check path to /.

instructions.text: ☐ Set the target-group health-check path to /.

instructions.text: ☐ Remove the ALB-source HTTP rule from fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg.

instructions.text: ☐ Confirm all changed rules match the original chain.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The original least-privilege configuration is restored.

tasks.title: Create baseline monitoring and an RDS manual snapshot
tasks.feature: Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon RDS backups
tasks.goal: Inspect native metrics, create a low-risk CloudWatch alarm without an action, and create one manual RDS snapshot for recovery practice.
tasks.whyItMatters: CloudWatch helps identify resource saturation and availability symptoms. RDS automated backups support point-in-time recovery within retention, while manual snapshots are retained until deleted. SAA-C03 questions mentioning recovery point objectives, point-in-time recovery, retained backups, or a user-initiated recovery copy should make you distinguish automated backups from manual snapshots.

consoleSteps.warning: Use eu-west-2 so that the metrics match the resources created by this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: You can inspect the EC2 CPU metric graph.
consoleSteps.warning: A low-traffic training workload might show little activity.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect ALB metrics
consoleSteps.expectedResult: You can inspect healthy-target capacity.
consoleSteps.warning: HealthyHostCount changes when targets become unhealthy or are deregistered.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect RDS metrics

consoleSteps.warning: No database connection attempt can legitimately leave this metric at zero.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-low-healthy-hosts --alarm-description "Training alarm for ALB healthy-host count" --namespace AWS/ApplicationELB --metric-name HealthyHostCount --dimensions Name=TargetGroup,Value=[TARGET_GROUP_DIMENSION] Name=LoadBalancer,Value=[LOAD_BALANCER_DIMENSION] --statistic Minimum --period 60 --evaluation-periods 1 --threshold 1 --comparison-operator LessThanThreshold --treat-missing-data breaching --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace the two metric-dimension placeholders with the TargetGroup and LoadBalancer dimension values shown by CloudWatch for this ALB. The command creates an alarm without an action.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The alarm is created in INSUFFICIENT_DATA or an evaluated state.
cliSteps.warning: Metric dimensions must exactly match the resource metric; do not invent dimension values.

cliSteps.command: aws rds create-db-snapshot --db-instance-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db --db-snapshot-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db-snap-001 --region eu-west-2

cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains a DB snapshot in creating state.
cliSteps.warning: A manual snapshot persists after DB deletion until you delete it.

cliSteps.expectedResult: The status progresses to available.
cliSteps.warning: Do not delete the DB instance until the snapshot is available if you intend to retain this recovery point.

verification.expectedResult: You have basic visibility into all three tiers.

verification.expectedResult: You can distinguish automated backups from the separate manual snapshot.

warnings.safety: This Follow Along permits inbound HTTP from 0.0.0.0/0 only on the temporary internet-facing ALB. Do not put passwords, access keys, secret values, or database connection strings in EC2 user data, CLI commands, browser pages, screenshots, or notes. When a MySQL login is required, use a password prompt and an administrator-approved secret-retrieval process without displaying the secret in this Follow Along.

findings.message: The supplied request requires creation of a dedicated IAM user, explicit IAM permissions, an EC2 instance role, and an instance profile. This package does not create IAM policies or trust policies because the protected instruction prohibits proposing an IAM policy. Use an administrator-approved, least-privilege learning identity and existing Session Manager-capable EC2 instance profile; have the administrator provision missing IAM resources outside this Follow Along.

The private RDS connectivity task includes an end-to-end TCP and optional password-prompted MySQL-login validation only when Systems Manager management, a MySQL client, and an approved secret-retrieval process already exist. The package intentionally does not retrieve, print, embed, or transmit database credentials.

The CloudWatch ALB HealthyHostCount CLI alarm requires exact CloudWatch TargetGroup and LoadBalancer dimension values from the learner account. Those values are represented as output-dependent placeholders rather than guessed.

RDS engine-version availability, DB instance-class availability, account quotas, subnet route tables, NAT availability, and whether an existing VPC has truly private database subnets must be confirmed in the learner account before resource creation.
